separable: inseparable — *ask for the check*, never ✗ *ask the check for*; the person you ask goes before the particle: *ask him for help*
gloss: To say that you want someone to give you something.
examples: *Ask for* a receipt when you pay.
She *asked for* two more days to finish the drawings.
He's *asking for* a raise at the review tomorrow.

separable: inseparable — the trouble follows the particle: *asking for trouble*, and in the fixed line *you asked for it*
gloss: To behave in a way that makes trouble certain to come.
examples: Riding at night with no lights is *asking for* trouble.
Nobody felt sorry for him — he *asked for* it.
She had *asked for* trouble the moment she took that shortcut.

separable: separable — *bat around a few ideas*, or *bat a few ideas around*; with a pronoun it must split: *bat it around*
gloss: To discuss an idea informally, without deciding anything yet.
examples: Let's *bat around* a few names for the new shop.
We *batted* the idea *around* for an hour and got nowhere.
They're still *batting around* possible dates for the trip.

ru: отказываться, отказаться (от приглашения, обязательства); отпрашиваться, отпроситься
separable: inseparable — *beg off the meeting*, never ✗ *beg the meeting off*; most often it takes no object at all: *he begged off*
transitivity: both — intransitive (she begged off), transitive (he begged off the trip)
gloss: To politely get out of something you had already agreed to do.
examples: He said he'd come, then *begged off* at the last minute.
I had to *beg off* the dinner because of work.
She has *begged off* three weekends in a row.

ru: выкипать, выкипеть; испаряться, испариться при кипении
separable: separable when it takes an object — *boil away the liquid*, *boil the liquid away*; most often it takes none: *the water boiled away*
transitivity: both — intransitive (the water boiled away), transitive (boil the extra liquid away)
gloss: To disappear completely by turning to steam.
examples: Turn the heat up and *boil* the extra liquid *away*.
Half the stock had *boiled away* by the time I came back.
The last of the water is *boiling away* now.

separable: separable — *boil down the sauce*, or *boil the sauce down*; with a pronoun it must split: *boil it down*
gloss: To cook a liquid until much of it evaporates and what is left is thicker.
examples: *Boil down* the syrup until it coats the back of a spoon.
She *boiled* the cream *down* by half.
The sauce has been *boiling down* for twenty minutes.

separable: separable — *boil down the report*, or *boil the report down*; with a pronoun it must split: *boil it down*
gloss: To shorten a long piece of writing or speech to its main points.
examples: Can you *boil down* this report for the board?
He *boiled* the whole argument *down* into three sentences.
I've *boiled down* my notes for you.

separable: inseparable — the feeling is the subject, not an object: *anger boiled up in him*, never ✗ *boil anger up*
gloss: For a strong feeling or a quarrel to grow and rise until it is hard to hold in.
examples: She could feel the anger *boil up* again.
Resentment *boiled up* between the two departments.
Something has been *boiling up* in that office for months.

separable: inseparable — *bomb out of the first round*, never ✗ *bomb the round out*
gloss: To fail badly and drop out of something, especially a contest.
examples: He *bombed out* in the first round of the tournament.
If we *bomb out* here, the season is over.
Two of the favorites have *bombed out* already.

separable: separable when it takes an object — *buck up the team*, and with a pronoun it must split: *buck them up*; most often it takes none: *buck up, it'll be fine*
transitivity: both — intransitive (buck up!), transitive (the news bucked us up)
gloss: To become more cheerful and determined, or to make someone feel that way.
examples: *Buck up* — the worst of it is behind us.
A phone call from his sister *bucked* him *up*.
The whole team has *bucked up* since the new coach arrived.

separable: inseparable — it takes no object at all: *tell him to buzz off*, never ✗ *buzz him off*
gloss: To go away, said rudely to someone you want to leave you alone.
examples: *Buzz off* and let me finish this.
The kids *buzzed off* as soon as the neighbor came outside.
I wish those two had *buzzed off* an hour ago.

separable: inseparable — *call forth a response*, not ✗ *call a response forth*
gloss: To cause a feeling or a reaction to appear.
examples: The photograph *called forth* memories he had buried for years.
A charge like that should *call forth* a full investigation.
The speech has *called forth* praise from both parties.

ru: доводить до конца, довести до конца; осуществлять, осуществить
separable: separable — *carry through the reform*, or *carry the reform through*; with a pronoun it must split: *carry it through*
gloss: To finish something you started, all the way to the end.
examples: The mayor promised the plan but never *carried* it *through*.
It takes stubbornness to *carry through* a project this long.
The reforms were finally *carried through* last spring.

ru: поддерживать, поддержать; помогать выстоять, помочь выстоять
separable: separable — the person goes in the middle: *carried her through*, *carried him through the worst of it*
gloss: For something to keep a person going through a hard time.
examples: Her sense of humor *carried* her *through* the whole ordeal.
A little savings will *carry* us *through* until payday.
That small pension is *carrying* them *through* the winter.

separable: separable — *cart off the old desks*, or *cart the old desks off*; with a pronoun it must split: *cart him off*
gloss: To take someone or something away roughly and without ceremony.
examples: The police *carted* him *off* in handcuffs.
Movers came at seven to *cart off* the old desks.
Everything of value had already been *carted off*.

ru: возвращать себе, вернуть себе; отбирать обратно, отобрать обратно
separable: separable — *claw back the bonuses*, or *claw the bonuses back*; with a pronoun it must split: *claw it back*
gloss: To get back money or ground that you had lost, and only with real effort.
examples: The company wants to *claw back* the bonuses it paid out.
We *clawed* most of the deficit *back* in the second half.
The state has *clawed back* millions in overpayments.

separable: separable — *clear away the plates*, or *clear the plates away*; with a pronoun it must split: *clear them away*
gloss: To take things off a surface and put them where they belong.
examples: I'll *clear away* the dishes if you make the coffee.
She *cleared* the papers *away* before the guests arrived.
The tables had all been *cleared away* by ten.
